newsitem.title: MEXICO: Top Mexican prosecutor killed in Tijuana.
newsitem.headline: Top Mexican prosecutor killed in Tijuana.

text.p: A top state prosecutor was shot dead and run over outside his home in the border town of Tijuana, officials said on Sunday.
Officials said the Friday slaying could have been revenge for major crimes Odin Armando Gutierrez was investigating, and drug that traffickers were suspected.
Some Mexican newspapers speculated that the killing could have been tied to his investigation of the 1994 murder of the area's public security director, Jose Frederico Benitez Lopez.
Benitez was killed soon after the March 23, 1994 assassination of ruling party presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio, which shook Mexico to its core.
But the federal attorney general's office denied that the killing was tied to the investigations of the Colosio murder.

In a statement released on Sunday, the federal attorney general's office said that Gutierrez was not scheduled to meet with a special federal prosecutor who was in Tijuana investigating the Colosio case.

Gutierrez arrived home in an upscale district of Tijuana late on Friday with his wife and daughter, who entered the house. As he parked the car, four men with AK-47 assault rifles fired more than 120 shots at Gutierrez. An autopsy showed the gunmen then ran over his body several times.
Gutierrez had been involved in investigating a number of sensitive crimes.
The government newspaper El Nacional reported that authorities suspect Gutierrez may have been killed by drug traffickers, who may also have murdered Benitez.
The daily Reforma said Gutierrez was also investigating the kidnapping of a Japanese businessman who was released unharmed after being abducted in Tijuana in August, 1996.
Tijuana, which is on the U.S. border, has been hit by a series of recent executions of leading public investigators.
The border city is the centre of operations of a powerful drugs cartel.
